findings.text: Well was completed as a Toolachee gas producer, not plugged; perforations 6388–6510 ft, re-completed 1992 with packers. No P&A record in the files read.
findings.quote: The well was cased and completed for gas production from the Toolachee with provision for later completion from the Namur Sandstone.

findings.text: 7in casing cement reported to 4300 ft, ~2000 ft above Toolachee top and over the Nappamerri seal; how the top was determined is not stated.
findings.quote: cemented with 630 sx of Class "F" cement with programmed additives. Cement top 4300' PBTD 6565'.

findings.text: Report maps independent closure with spill points directed into the higher Strzelecki Dome.
findings.quote: The Marabooka structure has independent closure at all prospective levels with well-defined spill points into the saddle.

findings.text: Report offers Toolachee–Patchawarra communication as one possible explanation for the water-wet Patchawarra.
findings.quote: (1) Communication between the Patchawarra and Toolachee at Marabooka;

findings.text: Driller and Schlumberger depths differ by 3–7 ft (e.g., Core 3 6392 vs 6399 ft); card uses wireline, narrative and casing tally use driller depths.
findings.quote: For Core and D.S.T. intervals Drillers Depths corrected to Log Depths wherever possible.

findings.text: 1981 and 1982 survey plans give longitudes ~8 arc-seconds (~220 m) apart and neither names a geodetic datum; confirm position before mapping.
Extrapolated static BHT is 267°F (~131°C) at 7157 ft; Toolachee DSTs recorded ~236°F (~113°C), relevant to CO₂ phase and well-material ratings.
The Nappamerri Formation lies directly above the Toolachee reservoir (top at 6,117 ft, about 1,864 m).

curves.label: Temperature vs depth (DST recorders + log BHT, report table)
curves.note: Digitised from table on PDF p264 (ft/°F converted). DST recorder and log temperatures are uncorrected except 7157 ft (extrapolated static BHT). DST 1 (120°F at 4681 ft, no recovery) omitted as anomalous.

notes: GA layer year 2005 disagrees with the report: spud 30 Dec 1980, rig release 30 Jan 1981, WCR dated May 1981. spudYear set from the report.
GA TD 2181 m matches driller TD 7156 ft (2181.1 m); logger TD is 7164 ft (2183.6 m).

Position: lat/lon kept from GA layer as briefed. Well card (1981) = −28.17756, 140.61119 (~200 m SE of GA); 1982 resurvey = −28.17747, 140.60897 (~210 m SW of GA). No geodetic datum stated on either plan; my unverified guess is GA = 1982 AMG position shifted to GDA94.

Elevations: 1981 plan GL 160.30 ft / KB 181.90 ft above MSL (Port Adelaide); 1982 plan GL 48.17x m AHD (last digit lost in scan noise) vs 48.86 m from 160.3 ft — ~0.7 m unresolved datum/levelling difference.
`page` = 1-based PDF page of the file. Stamped report numbers differ: +2 offset from PDF p10 onward; Volume 2 stamped page = PDF page − 227.
PBTD inconsistent: 6565 ft (drilling summary p21), 6563 ft (casing summary p274, 1984 diagram p321), 6555 ft (driller, 1992 diagram p322).
DST 3 condensate recovery: 433 ft in drilling narrative (p20) vs 443 ft on well card (p7) and conclusions (p31).
Formation tops list no Daralingie, Epsilon, Murteree, Tirrawarra or Merrimelia: Nappamerri (6117 ft) → Toolachee (6326) → Patchawarra (6526) → unnamed pre-Permian (7061).
Composite log header gives status 'COMPLETED GAS, SUSPENDED OIL'; well card says 'Completed Permian gas well, potential Namur Sandstone production'.
DST shut-in pressures on the card (p7) are partly overprinted by table rules; all marked low confidence. MPT pressure data (4100–7154 ft) not read.
No Government OCR docx in this package: ocrBaseline omitted, OCR stats zero.
/tmp writes are blocked in this environment; scratch crops were kept in a temporary folder inside marabooka-1/ and deleted at the end.
Counts describe the retained cloud evidence, not the complete original source package. Page counts cover included images, not every cited page.

findings.text: Granite below 4.1 km is very hot: 2003 PTS passes read 232–245 °C from 4130 to 4282 m MD; peak 244.7 °C.
Operator states 248 °C at 4389 m, below the PTS coverage; the measuring survey is not in this package.
By Sept 2005 the same depths read only 73–77 °C and recovered to ~167 °C over 16 h — injection-cooled, not reservoir temperature.
Pressure reached 10,915 psi (75.3 MPa) at 4282 m in 2003 — about 17.6 kPa/m, far above a fresh-water column.
2011 caliper: upper 1300 m of 4-1/2" tubing in good condition, no anomaly over 0.030"; deeper tubing and casing not inspected.
findings.quote: There are no obvious anomalies or any events that represent greater than 0.030" radial increase from the Max API spec.

findings.text: Lower completion compromised: NWJ packer failed pressure test, plug leaking (2009) and unretrievable (2014), coiled-tubing fish left in hole.
Well plugged and abandoned by 2016: bridge plug at 3032 m, cement plugs 2897–3032 m up to a 0–50 m surface plug.
Free gas in the shallow section: 100% methane recorded while drilling 254–650 m, relevant to any re-entry or nearby well.
findings.quote: 100% CH4 observed during drilling from 254m to 650m

curves.label: Temperature, PTS 3 Nov 2003, down pass 1 (best pass)
curves.note: TEMPI1D1, every 3rd 0.5-ft sample (+ last), depth ft × 0.3048, MD, datum not stated (other files use KB). Chosen: first pass into undisturbed fluid, steady ~60 ft/min, smooth, agrees with down pass 2 within 0.8 °C (up passes differ up to 3.9 °C). Labelled 'Injection 1' — may be cooled. ~6 °C jump between ~4252 and ~4267 m.

curves.label: Pressure, PTS 3 Nov 2003, down pass 1
curves.note: PRESI1D1 psi × 0.006894757; same depths as temperature curve; run labelled injection.

curves.label: Temperature, PTS in-run Sept 2005 (Ext sensor) — injection-cooled
curves.note: Ext, every 2nd 1-ft sample (+ last), ft × 0.3048. Shown for contrast only: ~165 °C colder than 2003; recovered to ~167 °C after 16 h (pts-2005-chart).

notes: Position from operator documents (dd-2014 p1 and caliper p7, identical DMS, datum not stated). GA Cooper borehole layer 'HABANERO 1' at 140.5696, -27.8266 (TD 3700 m, 2009) is 18.2 km away and conflicts on TD/year; other GA 'HABANERO' entries at lat -26.78 and -28.48 also do not match. OZTemp (GA) has Habanero 1 at 140.7544, -27.8158 — agrees with operator.
LAS 2003 files carry no date, location, service company or depth datum; the date is only in the file name. Curves are flagged I = INJECTION, so temperatures may be below static formation temperature.
2005 LAS: well 'Habenero 1', location 'Innaminka', DATE 09/24/2005 vs file name 23sept2005 and chart axis 23–24 Sep 2005. 2016 diagram spells 'Habenaro-1'. Name matching needs fuzzy rules.
7" shoe depth inconsistent within dd-2014: 4139.92 m (driller), 4140.1 m (loggers), 4134.92 m (casing table), 4134.7 m (remarks). 9-5/8" shoe 2250.03 m (diagrams) vs 2250.3 m (caliper header).
Tubing grade: SM95S (2003/2009/2014 diagrams) vs P110 (caliper report). Caliper p5 lists nominal ID 1.995" (p6: 3.50") and credits the nominal sizes to both Geodynamics and Santos.
No temperature data above 4101 m in this package: T at 3000 m and 4000 m rest on the operator's approximate "around 200 deg c" at the end of tubing (~3120 m) and are flagged low confidence.
INT_ (°F) and Int (°C) LAS curves are tool-internal (electronics flask) temperatures, not well temperatures — not used.
Caliper report pages 9–17 (well plot) and 25 (calibration image) were not reviewed beyond their text layer; stats count 25 pages sampled.
spudYear 2003 from casing-test dates in dd-2016 (FIT 19/02/2003 on 13-3/8" casing); the 2003 drilling rig was Century Rig 27 (dd-2014).
Depth reference: diagrams use MDRKB (RKB 73.71 m AHD, GL 65.30 m AHD). LAS depths are "Measured depth" with no datum; deviation <2° per dd-2014, so MD ≈ TVD within a few metres.
OCR baseline not applicable — all files are digital (text layers or LAS); ocr* counts are 0.
Page images rendered with pdfplumber page.to_image (pypdfium2); digital diagrams kept in colour, scans/charts as noted.

notes: Georeferencing from GeoTIFF tags (read with Pillow): ModelTiepoint pixel (0,0) → lon 112.92113549, lat -9.34304225; ModelPixelScale 0.05° × 0.05°; GeoKeys: geographic model, PixelIsArea, GDA94 (EPSG:4283), degrees. Full raster 814 × 686 px = [112.92114, -43.64304, 153.62114, -9.34304].

Crop = columns 481–781, rows 213–413 (301 × 201 native cells) snapped outward to the 0.05° grid; bounds [136.97113549, -30.04304225, 152.02113549, -19.99304225]. WebP is upscaled 4× with nearest-neighbour (1204 × 804) so cells stay crisp; it is plain lon/lat (equirectangular), so a Web-Mercator map should warp it or accept a small N–S stretch.

Pixel values are RGB, not °C. GA 'users help.txt': the TIFF/jpg colour stretch is 'a linear stretch between 85° and 235°'; 'maximum red' means 235 °C or greater. The image is a visual product, not a queryable grid.

Colour → °C: every non-black TIFF colour lies on GA's 3-segment ramp blue (0,0,255) → cyan (0,255,255) → yellow (255,255,0) → red (255,0,0) (max RGB distance 0.04). Ramp position t (0–1) → °C = 85 + 150·t. 121 colour classes, median width 1.18 °C (max 1.77 °C).

Legend check (scalebar_units.JPG, viewed + sampled): bar is linear in t; the '<85°' and '>235°' ticks fall at 85.1 and 235.3 °C, but the '160°' tick sits where the ramp gives 162.7 °C → treat converted values as ±3 °C, before any model error.
3% of valid cells in the crop are in GA's saturated top class (≥235 °C), including the Habanero, Marabooka and Moomba cells — the image cannot rank sites above 235 °C.

GA caveat (metadata/users help): continental-scale interpretation from BHTs extrapolated with 'a simplistic two layer geological model'; 'not appropriate to apply it at anything less than the broadest region scale'. Licence text in the download: 'Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Australia' (© Commonwealth of Australia (Geoscience Australia) 2010); credit line keeps CC BY 4.0 as briefed — check which applies.
No-data/ocean = RGB (0,0,0) in the TIFF → transparent (5.8% of the crop, the Coral Sea margin NE).

Well points: 9872 OZTemp records (3373 wells) inside lon 137–152, lat -30 to -20 (GDA94 Lat/Long (DD) columns). Reliable = 'Krig Flag' = Y (GA's flag; N = duplicate/unreliable) with a temperature and a depth: 9804 records, 3337 wells.
Per well: deepest reliable record; records within 10 m of the deepest are tie-broken by GA 'Temp Flag' = Y (GA's chosen record), then longest lag time, then highest temperature.
Thinning to ≤1200 points: kept the deepest well per 0.12° grid cell, plus every Innamincka, Habanero, Marabooka well and Moomba 1 → 1152 points.

Columns used (users help.txt): 'Depth of Temp (mGL)' = depth relative to surface, used when present, else 'Depth of Temp (m)' = 'usually a logger depth' (reference often unstated); 'Temperature (°C)' (many converted from °F; GA warns some conversions may be wrong); 'Method'+'Correction' → kind (most are uncorrected BHTs, which read low); 'Temperature Data_Source' → source.

Named records — HABANERO: Habanero 1 (SA1523): 4175.8 m, 220.56 °C, Wireline Log BHT; Habanero 1 (SA1523): 4157.5 m, 202.78 °C, Wireline Log BHT (Uncorrected), lag 17.5 h; Habanero 2 (SA1524): 3925.8 m, 202.78 °C, Wireline Log BHT (Uncorrected), lag 23.5 h, TempFlag Y.

Named records — INNAMINCKA: 37 records in 4 wells; chosen point per well: Innamincka 1 3851 m 138.0 °C (Unknown); Innamincka 2 3356 m 151.7 °C (Wireline Log (BHT) (Uncorrected)); Innamincka 3 2843 m 136.1 °C (Horner Plot (Horner A)); Innamincka 4 2124 m 122.0 °C (Unknown (Corrected?)). Innamincka 1 temps are from Howard (1963), method 'Unknown'.

Named records — MARABOOKA: 21 records in 5 wells; chosen point per well: Marabooka 1 2174 m 131.0 °C (Unknown (Corrected?)); Marabooka 2 2216 m 136.0 °C (Unknown (Corrected?)); Marabooka 3 2180 m 134.0 °C (Unknown (Corrected?)); Marabooka 4 2228 m 126.0 °C (Unknown (Corrected?)); Marabooka 5 2270 m 113.3 °C (Wireline Log BHT (Uncorrected)).
Named records — MOOMBA: 372 records in 132 wells (Moomba 1–137 with gaps, Moomba North 1–2, Moomba South 1, Moomba 18 DW1). Moomba 1 (SA1508): 2892 m 178.0 °C Unknown (Geotherm94).
Name trap: 'Moombah 1' (QLD0337, Bowen Basin, QLD, lat -27.932, lon 149.132; 1779 m, 60.0 °C) is a different well ~870 km east of Moomba — do not match on name.
ZEROGEN: no records in the OZTemp extract (searched 'ZERO'/'ZG').
Full list of named records is in 'namedRecords' (extra key, not in the brief's shape).

context.name: Moomba CCS
context.tag: CO₂ storage project · operating since 2024 · Cooper Basin, SA
context.positionNote: Marker placed at the Moomba 1 well (Geoscience Australia borehole layer) as a locator for the Moomba gas plant.

facts.text: Moomba CCS captures CO₂ at the Moomba gas plant and stores it in depleted reservoirs in the Cooper Basin.
facts.source: Santos — Moomba Carbon Capture and Storage

facts.text: The CO₂ travels about 50 km by pipeline to the storage site.
facts.source: Santos — Moomba Carbon Capture and Storage

facts.text: Operating since September 2024, it had stored more than 2 million tonnes of CO₂e as of May 2026.
facts.source: Santos — Moomba Carbon Capture and Storage

facts.text: Its monitoring and verification plan includes monitoring the integrity of the wells.
facts.source: Santos — Moomba Carbon Capture and Storage
